analysis: The change is documentation-only (docs/architecture/inference.md). It adds head lines 25-171 describing the unregistered Nemotron Super local owner and one edit near line 868 about the shared media discovery policy. No code or controls change. The doc states: no model registration or HTTP route; the optional NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP hook is authenticated, defaults absent and has no production caller. Inputs are bounded (ingress, media and decode charges; PNG/JPEG data URIs only; 429 on queue-full). Memory is reserved for the prefill lane, the checkpoint bank and MTP, and charges are retained on native faults. MTP is opt-in (DARKBLOOM_NEMOTRON_SUPER_MTP=1) and rejects media. Security-relevant gap: the new resident checkpoint-bank prefix cache (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1) uses a local unscoped cache scope. T-041 asserts there is no production RAM tier and that scope is coordinator-authored. This is harmless while the path is unwired, but T-041 needs a note. The rewrite at ~line 868 says multimodal template-render fixtures follow the media discovery policy instead of vision_config. That relates to the TemplateRenderCheck behavior, which is not in the supplied evidence. Not verified: any code behind the cited Swift paths, the real default for DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY, and whether anything outside this doc registers the owner. The line citation for the finding is estimated from hunk counting.

findings.detail: The new section describes an owner-resident recurrent checkpoint bank, enabled by DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_MEMORY=1. Text requests use it with "the local unscoped cache scope". T-041 states that production never constructs a resident-RAM prefix cache and that cacheSalt is coordinator-authored per account, model build and prompt contract. The doc says this path is unregistered, has no production caller, and exposes no route. As written it is not a regression. But if the Nemotron Super owner or its local HTTP hook (NemotronSuperLocalImageHTTP) is ever wired to coordinator or multi-tenant traffic, requests would share one scope. That would reopen the cross-account TTFT oracle that T-041 and SEC-035 treat as closed. The checkpoint bank would also add RAM-resident prompt-derived state outside the SSD tier's HMAC, TTL and KEK controls. T-041 should be updated to say this tier is local-only and unscoped, and that wiring it to coordinator traffic requires a fresh sign-off with coordinator-supplied cacheSalt.
findings.title: Docs add a resident-RAM, unscoped prefix-cache path that T-041 says does not exist
